subsystems.name: Target body and anchoring
subsystems.role: the asteroid itself is the raw material and the radiation shield; equipment must hold station on a body with almost no gravity.
parts: harpoons or pitons for a loose surface

subsystems.name: Excavation and material handling
subsystems.role: hollows out the interior and processes the spoil.

subsystems.name: Spin-up system
subsystems.role: spins the body by throwing excavated rock or firing thrusters, and later trims the rate.

subsystems.name: Pressure shell and structure
subsystems.role: makes the cavity gas-tight and takes the loads from spin and internal pressure.
parts: sealed liner (metal, composite or cast basalt)
hoop reinforcement cables or wound bands

subsystems.name: Interior fit-out
subsystems.role: turns a cavity into habitable volume.
parts: decks and floors stacked along the spin axis

subsystems.name: Power and life support
subsystems.role: keeps people alive and the shell pressurised for years.

buildSteps.title: Find and characterise a body
buildSteps.detail: Telescopes and a rendezvous probe map shape, spin state, internal structure and composition. Most small near-Earth asteroids are loose rubble piles rather than solid rock, which changes every later step.

buildSteps.title: Rendezvous and anchor
buildSteps.detail: In near-zero gravity, mining equipment cannot simply sit on the surface; it must be bolted, netted or thrust-clamped to the body, or operate from a free-flying platform alongside it.

buildSteps.title: Mine the interior
buildSteps.detail: Tunnels are cut inward and the excavated rock is stockpiled. If the body is a weak aggregate, tunnelling may be replaced by containing and compacting it rather than carving it.

buildSteps.title: Build the pressure shell
buildSteps.detail: A gas-tight liner is installed against the cavity walls and reinforced with tension members — cable hoops, wound bands or imported composite — because rock has almost no tensile strength.

buildSteps.title: Spin it up slowly
buildSteps.detail: Mass drivers throw spoil off tangentially, or thrusters apply torque, until the inner surface reaches the target gravity. Accidental tumbling must be damped throughout, and the shell must survive the loads.

buildSteps.title: Pressurise and test
buildSteps.detail: The cavity is filled with breathable gas at roughly half an atmosphere and leak-tested; internal pressure adds hoop stress comparable to the spin load on a shell this large.

buildSteps.title: Fit out the interior
buildSteps.detail: Decks, power, life support, workshops and growing areas are installed, with heavy equipment placed low and the axis left open for docking.

buildSteps.title: Operate and maintain
buildSteps.detail: Spin rate, gas composition, shielding thickness and structural strain are monitored continuously over decades; water and carbon are recycled from the remaining asteroid material.

prerequisites.why: sample-return missions have touched and characterised asteroids, but nobody has yet extracted material and kept it working in space.
drilling, holding position and moving spoil on a tumbling, near-weightless body is untested.
space station modules exist at tens of metres, not the hundreds of metres needed for useful artificial gravity.
anything above a couple of rotations per minute tends to make people motion-sick; at that rate, one g needs a radius of roughly 220 m.
station systems already recycle most water and some air, but not food or long-term reliability over decades.
running a habitat, mining tools and spin-up hardware needs far more power than current spacecraft generate.

pathway.milestone: sample-return missions to near-Earth asteroids (Hayabusa2 in 2020, OSIRIS-REx in 2023)
pathway.unlocks: ground truth on rubble-pile structure, volatiles and regolith behaviour.

pathway.milestone: robotic prospecting and small extraction demonstrations on a single asteroid
pathway.unlocks: proven anchoring, digging and volatile processing in microgravity.

pathway.milestone: an uncrewed test cavity — mined, lined, sealed and pressurised at a few metres scale, possibly as a free-flying structure built from asteroid material rather than a hollowed body
pathway.unlocks: real data on sealing, leak rates and hoop loads before people are involved.

pathway.milestone: a crewed outpost inside a small spun body at partial gravity, then a full one-g habitat a few hundred metres across
pathway.unlocks: settlement volume whose shielding and structure were never launched from Earth — if the tensile-strength and life-support problems can be solved.
